answer: Pay graders only after a hidden second panel, drawn from distant corners of the trust graph, rescores the same work. A farm can stack cheap identities on the wharf like timber, but each clone then needs a record of agreeing with strangers it cannot predict or bribe. A grader who calls a clumsy sonnet a 3 while independent panels call it a 1 forfeits part of its bond, so extra clones cost money instead of compounding influence.
